brief: Early stone miner's house (c.1828 per HABS) built into a hillside: a two-storey side-gabled block of rough-coursed local limestone with a metal-sheathed roof, big stone end chimneys, shuttered 6/6 windows and a small gabled hood on turned brackets over the door, with a lower stone and frame lean-to and a board picket fence along the walk.

facade.notes: a two-storey rubble-stone house with dressed quoins and lintels, a side-gabled metal roof and big end chimneys, louvred shutters; a lean-to hood on brackets over the door; a lower stone wing to one side; a picket fence along the sidewalk; the hill rises steeply behind with sheds

why.note: Cornish lead miners built in local limestone (Mineral Point, 1830s-40s)
a picket fence on the street line: the front-yard fence of the pre-1900 town
